package_info.why_malicious: The SHARPTEXT browser extension is explicitly designed to steal webmail credentials and session data from Gmail and AOL users. It leverages browser APIs to intercept authentication cookies and exfiltrate them to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The extension has no legitimate functionality and its sole purpose is credential theft, making the entire package malicious.

execution_context.trigger: While the user is actively browsing Gmail or AOL webmail (runtime event-driven)
execution_context.file_location: background.js (core background script of the extension)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user accesses Gmail or AOL webmail, the code intercepts completed web requests to these domains, collects associated session cookies using the cookies API, and transmits this data to an attacker-controlled server via network request, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code actively monitors web requests to high-value webmail domains and programmatically extracts session cookies, which are then sent to an external server. This behavior is a hallmark of credential theft and is never required for legitimate browser extension functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions should not access or transmit authentication cookies or session data for webmail services to any third party. Accessing such sensitive data and exfiltrating it violates user privacy and browser security policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers or security tools may access login forms or cookies for autofill or security checks, but they do not transmit this data to external servers without explicit user consent and never for unrelated domains.
key_indicators: Use of webRequest and cookies APIs to target mail.google.com and mail.aol.com
Extraction of authentication/session cookies from browser storage
Outbound network requests from extension code to non-standard, attacker-controlled domains
References to webmail domains in background.js or manifest.json

attack_chain.action: User is deceived into installing the SHARPTEXT browser extension from a web store or phishing link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious extension is installed and active in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: The extension monitors browser activity and intercepts web requests to Gmail and AOL webmail domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of session cookies or authentication credentials from the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: The extension exfiltrates the stolen session cookies or credentials to an attacker-controlled server via network requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the victim's webmail accounts using the stolen session data.

behavioral_signatures: Browser extension requesting webRequest and cookies permissions and monitoring traffic to mail.google.com or mail.aol.com
Extension code extracting session cookies for webmail domains
Outbound network requests from extension context to external, non-standard domains, especially after webmail access
file_indicators: manifest.json requesting webRequest, cookies, tabs, and activeTab permissions
background.js or content scripts containing references to mail.google.com or mail.aol.com
Code patterns that extract cookies and perform network POST requests
network_indicators: Outbound connections from browser extension to attacker-controlled domains or IP addresses not associated with legitimate webmail services
Unusual POST requests containing session cookie values or authentication tokens originating from extension background scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installed browser extensions for excessive or unnecessary permissions (webRequest, cookies, tabs, activeTab). Scan extension scripts for code referencing webmail domains (mail.google.com, mail.aol.com) and for functions that extract cookies. Inspect network traffic for suspicious outbound connections initiated by extensions, especially POST requests containing authentication data to unknown domains. Flag extensions that combine these behaviors for further investigation.
